attacks.claim: The artifact does not say what happens when app 9.2 edits a schedule that also has a v2 (8-period) copy. 9.2 can edit 4-period schedules, so a 9.2 edit could leave a stale v2 that 4.8 later reads.
attacks.evidence: App 9.2 and older can view but not edit 8-period schedules; ABSENT: behaviour when 9.2 edits a schedule that already has a v2 copy

attacks.claim: Editing on 4.7 permanently discards the user's 8-period schedule, and the artifact describes this as a normal path with no user notice. This is silent data loss.
attacks.evidence: When a unit on 4.7 edits its schedule, the cloud discards the stale v2 copy, so a later re-upgrade starts from the current v1 schedule

attacks.claim: The downgrade message does not say which periods were dropped or what the new schedule is, so users cannot check the result.
attacks.evidence: The app shows 'Some schedule changes were simplified' if v2 had more than 4 periods

attacks.claim: Home/Away deletion is promised for the 7-day store and on toggle-off, but the same events also feed telemetry ingest. The artifact gives no retention or deletion for that copy.
attacks.evidence: Home/Away state adds ~1 small event per state change; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest; ABSENT: retention and deletion for the telemetry copy

attacks.claim: Timestamped Home/Away transitions tied to an account can reconstruct a household's occupancy pattern. The artifact treats the data as minimal without addressing that linkability.
attacks.evidence: Only the resulting Home/Away state is sent to the cloud (needed to show it in the app); it is kept 7 days

attacks.claim: Schedules and Home/Away state depend on the vendor cloud. The artifact gives no self-host, export, or exit path for user data.
attacks.evidence: the cloud stores both [schedule versions]; ABSENT: export or self-host path for schedules and Home/Away history

attacks.claim: Stage 4 is open-ended with no pacing, and all units install inside the same 02:00-05:00 local window. The artifact does not show that the OTA service and CDN can absorb a 612k-unit burst.
attacks.evidence: | 4 | 100% | — | — |; Install window 02:00-05:00 local

attacks.claim: Egress counts one image pass per unit. Retries, re-downloads, and a full revert push (another ~1.5 TB) are not counted, and the telemetry cost is given only as a percentage.
attacks.evidence: OTA egress: 2.4 MB image × 612k units ≈ 1.5 TB; projected +0.4% on telemetry ingest

attacks.claim: The claim that freeze/heat protection is never interrupted conflicts with the install design, which holds relays off for about 90 s. The artifact also does not say how long the 3 failed boots take before auto-revert, so relays could stay dark for an unknown period.
attacks.evidence: During the ~90 s install, relays are held open (off); so freeze/heat protection is never interrupted; ABSENT: duration of each boot attempt before auto-revert

attacks.claim: The stage gate depends on HVAC fault telemetry, but the pager does not alert on HVAC fault codes or support-contact spikes. A 4.8 regression in HVAC behaviour could pass stage 1 unseen and page no one.
attacks.evidence: Pages firmware on-call if boot reverts exceed 0.1% of updated units in any 6 h window or offline rate rises 0.5 points over baseline

attacks.claim: The revert is itself an OTA install, so it inherits the 02:00-05:00 window, the indoor-temperature deferral with no stated upper bound, and up to 14 days of user postponement. Revert latency is not quantified, which weakens the agreed guarantee that devices can always return to the previous firmware.
attacks.evidence: Users can postpone an update up to 14 days from the app; Install is deferred if indoor temperature is below 7 °C; Revert: push 4.7 to updated units through the same OTA path

attacks.claim: The energy claim is public and load-bearing, but the artifact gives no control arm, no variance or interval, and no proof that the 2025-26 trial ran the same Away Assist thresholds that ship.
attacks.evidence: cut heating runtime by a median of 6%; ABSENT: control design, dispersion, and firmware or algorithm version used in the trial

attacks.claim: At stage 1 the 0.05% boot-revert gate is roughly 3 units out of 6,100, which is too little signal to advance on. The gate also has no threshold for schedule-sync or Away Assist errors.
attacks.evidence: boot-revert rate < 0.05%; Stage 1: 1% (~6,100)

attacks.claim: The HIL test description lists 'no C-wire power stealing' as a tested configuration, which is ambiguous. Power-stealing installs are the case where relays held off and flash writes could brown out, and the artifact does not show they were tested.
attacks.evidence: HIL bench: conventional 1H/1C, 2-stage, heat pump + aux, no C-wire power stealing; ABSENT: explicit power-stealing install results

attacks.claim: The on-device Away Assist settings and display are not covered by the accessibility or UI tests, which cover only the app.
attacks.evidence: App 9.3 schedule editor and Away Assist screens with VoiceOver, TalkBack, 200% text; ABSENT: device-display Away Assist UI test

attacks.claim: Public copy implies a 6% heating saving for users, but Away Assist is off by default, so most users will not get that benefit without opting in.
attacks.evidence: cut heating runtime by a median of 6%; Away Assist (optional, off by default)

attacks.claim: The release notes promise rollout over two weeks, but stages 1-3 take about 11 days and stage 4 has no end. Users who postpone up to 14 days will receive the update on an unpredictable timeline.
attacks.evidence: Rolling out over the next two weeks; Users can postpone an update up to 14 days

attacks.claim: Away Assist sets heating to Away setpoints automatically. The artifact does not show that users with limited mobility or who need to override it can do so from the device as well as the app.
attacks.evidence: ABSENT: device-side override or accessibility test for Away Assist behaviour

attacks.claim: Dual-writing v1 and v2 on every edit, plus cloud-side discard rules, creates hidden coupling between firmware, cloud, and app versions. This is hard to test across the 4.7, 4.8, 9.2, and 9.3 matrix.
attacks.evidence: 4.8 ... also writes a v1 schedule (4 periods) on every edit, keeping the 4 periods closest to the user's wake / leave / return / sleep anchors; the cloud stores both

attacks.claim: The energy claim is published on stage 1 and cannot be recalled, but the artifact shows only a reference number for legal substantiation, not the outcome. Away Assist also adds a new occupancy data category, and the artifact does not show the legal outcome for that category.
attacks.evidence: reviewed by legal for substantiation, LGL-4472; Privacy notice section 3 updated (legal review LGL-4471)

attacks.claim: Anti-rollback is intentionally left open, so any previously signed image can be installed. The artifact asserts 4.8 has no security fixes but does not confirm that 4.7 has no open security issues a downgrade would reintroduce.
attacks.evidence: 4.8 does not increment the secure-boot anti-rollback counter (no security fixes in this release), so 4.7 remains installable; ABSENT: confirmation 4.7 has no open security issues

attacks.claim: Away Assist treats two hours without motion as absence and lowers heating to the Away setpoint. Still or sleeping occupants, including elderly or ill people, can be misclassified as away, and the artifact describes no minimum-temperature floor or sensor-fault fallback.
attacks.evidence: the thermostat's built-in motion sensor sets Away mode after 2 h with no motion during scheduled 'home' periods; ABSENT: minimum floor and sensor-fault behaviour

attacks.claim: The employee beta (employees' own homes) is not representative of the fleet, so 'no increase in support contacts' is weak evidence for a fleet-wide release.
attacks.evidence: Employee beta: 1,140 homes for 3 weeks; no increase in support contacts
